\section{SCIANTIX status}
% =====================================================================

\begin{frame}{SCIANTIX had three formation models for the restructured volume fraction}
  \begin{center}
  \small
  \begin{tabular}{lll}
    \toprule
    option & form & driven by \\
    \midrule
    1 & KJMA, Barani (2020)\footnotemark[1] & effective burnup \\
    2 & KJMA $+$ $bu_{\text{inc}} = 15$, Biswas and Aagesen (2025)\footnotemark[2] & effective burnup \\
    3 & KJMA on $\rho_d$, Veshchunov\footnotemark[3] + Zullo (2026) & local burnup \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
  \end{center}

  \vspace{0.4em}
  All three are \alert{transformation kinetics}: a sigmoid fitted in burnup. None of them produces
    the \textbf{mean misorientation} $\Theta$ of the subgrains, or the \textbf{subgrain radius} $r_n$.

  \footnotetext[1]{Barani \emph{et al.}, \emph{J.\ Nucl.\ Mater.} \textbf{539} (2020) 152296.}
  \footnotetext[2]{Biswas and Aagesen, \emph{Comput.\ Mater.\ Sci.} \textbf{258} (2025) 114052, Eq.\ 45.}
  \footnotetext[3]{Veshchunov and Shestak, \emph{J.\ Nucl.\ Mater.} \textbf{384} (2009) 12--18.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{The data this model is built on}
  \small
  
  \begin{center}
  \footnotesize
  \begin{tabular}{llccc}
    \toprule
    paper & technique & $\Theta$ & $X$ & $r_n$ \\
    \midrule
    Zacharie-Aubrun (2022), standard UO$_2$ & EBSD                         & 27 & 27 & 14 \\
    Zacharie-Aubrun (2022), Cr-doped        & EBSD                         & 11 & 11 &  8 \\
    Onofri (2025)                           & EBSD, no restructuring ($\Theta = 0$) & 14 & -- & -- \\
    Gerczak (2018)                          & image analysis (Barani 2020), $d_A/2$ & -- &  5 &  4 \\
    Noirot (2015)                           & Xe-depleted area                &  -- &  6 & -- \\
    \midrule
    \textbf{total}                          &                              & \textbf{52} & \textbf{49} & \textbf{26} \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
  \end{center}

  \footnotesize
  $\Theta = [\,A_{\text{Mis}}(f_1-f_{10}) + 10 f_{10}\,]/100$; \quad
  
  $X = f_{10}$, area fraction above $10^\circ$; \quad
  
  $r_n = \text{ECD50}\,\%/2$.

  $1^\circ$ is the lower bin edge of the EBSD data.
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
\begin{frame}{What KJMA is, and what it assumes}
  Nuclei appear \emph{at random} in the untransformed material and grow \emph{isotropically};
  count the transformed volume as if the growing regions could overlap freely, the
  \alert{extended volume} $V_e$, and the overlap correction is statistical:
  \[ \mathrm{d}X = \Big(1 - X\Big)\,\frac{\mathrm{d}V_e}{V}
     \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
     X = 1 - \exp\!\big(-K\,t^{\,n}\big) \]

  \begin{columns}[T]
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      \textbf{What you get}\\
      \small
      $K$ and $n$, and a sigmoid. $n$ carries the dimensionality of growth
      and the nucleation regime.
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
      \textbf{What it assumes}\\
      \small
      Randomly placed nuclei, a growth law independent of where you are in the
      transformation, and a \emph{time dependence}.
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}

\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
\begin{frame}{The time dependence in the KJMA model}
  \small
  \begin{itemize}
    \item[\textbf{1}] \textbf{Effective burnup}, $n = 3.54$, $K = 2.77\times10^{-7}$, fitted on
      restructured-fraction data. 
    \item[\textbf{2}] Same, with an \textbf{incubation burnup} $bu_{\text{inc}} = 15$\,MWd/kgHM
      below which nothing happens. Biswas \& Aagesen get it from a balance between the energy
      stored in dislocations and the energy of forming a subgrain used to shift the origin of an empirical curve rather than to
      build the curve.
    \item[\textbf{3}] KJMA not on burnup but on the \textbf{dislocation density}
      $\rho_d(bu,T)$, with a threshold $\rho_{\text{crit}} = 6\times10^{14}$\,m$^{-2}$.
      The first to make the driver a \textbf{microstructural state variable} and the only one 
       that feels temperature.
  \end{itemize}

  \begin{block}{What none of them can do}
    They are calibrated on $X$ alone. There is no misorientation angle neither subgrain size.
  \end{block}
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
\begin{frame}{Why a phase transition could be the right shape for this problem}
  \begin{columns}
    \begin{column}{0.35\textwidth}
      \textbf{The HBS forms \emph{continuously}}

      \small
      Not by nucleating new grains, but by low-angle boundaries absorbing dislocations until
      their misorientation drifts through the $10^\circ$ HAGB threshold. In the metallurgical
      literature this is \emph{continuous} dynamic recrystallization, and it is a well-posed
      alternative to the nucleation-and-growth picture KJMA describes.\footnotemark[5]

    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.6\textwidth}
      \textbf{A continuous transformation has an order parameter}

      \small
      If a single continuous quantity distinguishes the two states, Landau's argument applies: write the energy as a function of it and keep only what symmetry allows.\footnotemark[6]
      \[ F(\eta) = \rho_{\text{free}}\,A_1\,Gb^2 + \rho_{\text{ord}}(\eta)\,A_2(\eta)\,Gb^2 \]

      $F$ depends on $\eta$ only through $\eta^2$ and $|\eta|$: the energy of a boundary cannot
      depend on the \emph{sign} of the misorientation across it. 

      \vspace{0.4em}
      $F$ has no threshold of its own: every length in it scales with the density. The
      threshold comes from the critical density $\rho_{\text{crit}}$ in $\rho_{\text{tot}}$.
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}

  \footnotetext[5]{Gourdet \& Montheillet, \emph{Acta Mater.} \textbf{51} (2003) 2685;
    Humphreys, Rohrer \& Rollett (2017), chs.\ 6 and 10.}
  \footnotetext[6]{Landau (1937); Landau \& Lifshitz, \emph{Statistical Physics} I, \S143.}
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
\begin{frame}{Landau against KJMA, side by side}
  \begin{center}
  \small
  \begin{tabular}{p{0.30\textwidth}p{0.30\textwidth}p{0.30\textwidth}}
    \toprule
     & KJMA (options 1--3) & Landau (option 4) \\
    \midrule
    what is solved      & a \emph{kinetic} law along a path & the \emph{equilibrium} of a state \\
    driver              & burnup or $\rho$ threshold      & $\rho_{\text{tot}}(bu)-\rho_{\text{crit}}$ \\
    free parameters     & $K$, $n$ fitted on $X$             & $\beta$, $k$, $\rho_{\text{crit}}$ fitted jointly on $\Theta$, $X$, $r_n$ \\
    predicts $X$        & by construction                    & \good{yes}, lever rule, no extra parameter \\
    predicts $\Theta$, $r_n$ & no                            & \good{yes} \\
    reversible?         & no, by construction                & yes, see below \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
  \end{center}

  \begin{block}{The price of using an equilibrium theory}
    A drop in $\rho_{\text{tot}}$ would un-restructure
    the fuel. Restructuring is irreversible, so the implementation carries a \alert{monotonic lock} on $\Theta$. However, this is easy if one considers the dislocation density generated by irradiation, and
    eventually includes the annealing phenomena within the evolution of the Landau free energy.
  \end{block}
\end{frame}


% =====================================================================
\section{The model}
% =====================================================================

\begin{frame}{HBS as a second-order phase transition}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
      \textbf{Order parameter}
      \[ \eta = \frac{\theta}{\theta_{\max}}, \qquad
         \theta_{\max} \equiv \theta_{\text{HAGB}} = 10^\circ \]
      the mean misorientation normalised to the LAGB/HAGB boundary.

      \vspace{0.5em}
      \textbf{External condition:} the local burnup, entering \emph{only} through the
      dislocation density available to polygonize
      \[ \rho_{\text{tot}}(bu) = \max\!\big(10^{\,2.2\times10^{-2}\,bu\,+\,13.8}-\rho_{\text{crit}},\,0\big) \]
      \hfill\footnotesize Nogita \& Une (1994)
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.46\textwidth}
      \textbf{Free energy}
      \[ F(\eta) = \rho_{\text{free}}A_1Gb^2 + \rho_{\text{ord}}A_2Gb^2 \]
      Even in $\eta$: the energy cannot depend on the \emph{sign} of a misorientation.

      \vspace{0.5em}
      Minimising $F$ gives $\Theta$; the same wall geometry gives $r_n$;
      the lever rule gives $X$.

      \vspace{0.5em}
      \begin{block}{Three adjustable parameters}
        $\beta$ (wall geometry), $k$ (sweeping), $\rho_{\text{crit}}$ (critical density,
        the density scale $F$ lacks).
      \end{block}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{The geometric wall}
  A low-angle boundary \emph{is} a wall of dislocations.
  \vspace{0.5em}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      \textbf{1. Spacing sets the angle} \quad $\theta = b/d$

      so a wall of $n$ dislocation families carries a line length per unit \emph{wall area}
      \[ L_A = n\theta/b \]

      \textbf{2. Wall area per unit volume or low angle grain boundary surface}
      \[ S/V = 3\sqrt{\rho_{\text{LAGB}}}\,/\,\beta \]
      \footnotesize $\beta$: the one geometric parameter, of the same kind as Rest \& Hofman (2000) but written on $\rho_{\text{LAGB}}$, not on the total network density. $n = 2$, Gourdet \& Montheillet, not fitted (between 1-3).
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
      \textbf{Close the two on each other:}
      $\rho_{\text{LAGB}} = L_A \cdot S/V$
      \[ \Longrightarrow\quad \sqrt{\rho_{\text{LAGB}}} = \frac{3n\theta}{\beta b} \]

      \begin{block}{Everything follows from $\theta$ alone}
        \[ \rho_{\text{LAGB}} = \Big(\tfrac{3n\theta}{\beta b}\Big)^{2},
           \qquad r_n = \min\!\Big(\frac{1.5}{(S/V)\,e^{-x}},\,R_{\text{grain}}\Big) \]
        with $S/V = 9n\theta/(\beta^{2}b)$ and $x$ the extended swept volume (next slide).
      \end{block}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{The dislocation balance}
  Every dislocation is in exactly one of three states, and they must \alert{add up to
  $\rho_{\text{tot}}$}. With the extended swept volume $x = k\,\rho_{\text{ord}}/\rho_{\text{tot}}$
  (Gourdet \& Montheillet: $d\rho_i = -\rho_i\,dV$, integrated):
  \[
    \underbrace{\rho_{\text{ord}} = \rho^{\max}_{\text{LAGB}}\,\eta^{2}}_{\text{condensed into low-angle walls}}
    \;+\;
    \underbrace{(\rho_{\text{tot}}-\rho_{\text{ord}})\big(1-e^{-x}\big)}_{\rho_{\text{swept}}:\ \text{annihilated by moving boundaries}}
    \;+\;
    \underbrace{(\rho_{\text{tot}}-\rho_{\text{ord}})\,e^{-x}}_{\rho_{\text{free}}:\ \text{still a random array}}
    \;=\; \rho_{\text{tot}}
  \]

  Each population carries the line energy of the state it is in:
  \[
    F \;=\; \rho_{\text{free}}\,A_1\,G b^2 \;+\; \rho_{\text{ord}}\,A_2\,G b^2,
    \qquad A_i = \frac{f(\nu)}{4\pi}\ln\frac{R_i}{b}
  \]
  \vspace{-0.9em}

  \[ A_1 = \tfrac{f(\nu)}{4\pi}\ln\frac{\rho_{\text{tot}}^{-1/2}}{b},\qquad
     A_2(\eta) = \tfrac{f(\nu)}{4\pi}\ln\frac{\min(b/\theta,\;\rho_{\text{tot}}^{-1/2})}{b} \]

  the swept ones carry nothing. Here $x$ is a \emph{volume}: a linear $\Delta R/R$ form would
  differ ($x \approx 0.5$ at 60\,GWd/tU, $e^{-x}=0.6$ against $1-x=0.5$).
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{The functional, collected}
  \[
    F = C_0 + E_{\text{wall}} + E_{\text{sweep}},
    \qquad C_0 = \rho_{\text{tot}} A_1 G b^2
  \]
  \[
    E_{\text{wall}} = \underbrace{\rho_{\text{ord}}(A_2 - A_1)\,Gb^2}_{\le 0:\ \text{the screening gain}},
    \qquad
    E_{\text{sweep}} = \underbrace{-\,\rho_{\text{swept}}\, A_1 Gb^2}_{\le 0:\ \text{annihilation}}
  \]

  \vspace{0.5em}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      \textbf{The engine of the transition} is $A_2 - A_1$.
      As burnup rises, $\rho_{\text{tot}}$ rises, the screening length due to wall formation shrinks, $A_2$ falls below $A_1$, and it becomes cheaper to store dislocations in walls than to leave them random.
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      \textbf{Equilibrium}: minimum of $F$ on $[0,\min(\eta_{\text{bal}},1)]$,
      by a coarse scan and a golden section ($A_2$ carries $\theta\ln\theta$ and the sweep an
      exponential: no closed form). Both terms are negative from $\eta=0$ on, so the threshold
      is $\rho_{\text{crit}}$ in $\rho_{\text{tot}}$, and it is continuous.
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Condition on the minimisation problem: dislocation balance}
  The walls cannot hold more dislocations than exist, so
  $\rho_{\text{ord}} \leq \rho_{\text{tot}}$. The equilibrium is the minimum of $F$ on the
  \alert{admissible interval}, not the free stationary point:

  \begin{block}{Eq.~(7b) --- admissibility}
    \[
      \eta_{\text{bal}} = \sqrt{\min\!\left(\frac{\rho_{\text{tot}}}{\rho^{\max}_{\text{LAGB}}},\,1\right)},
      \qquad
      \eta_{\text{eq}} = \operatorname*{argmin}_{[0,\,\min(\eta_{\text{bal}},1)]} F
    \]
  \end{block}

  \small
  With the current calibration the bound \alert{binds at high burnup, from 89 to 110\,GWd/tU}
  (600\,K), where every dislocation is in a wall and $\Theta = \beta b\sqrt{\rho_{\text{tot}}}/3n$.
  Below that the minimum is interior.
\end{frame}

\section{Calibration}
% =====================================================================

\begin{frame}{The objective and the three data sets}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      Joint fit of $\beta, k, \rho_c$ ($n = 2$ fixed) on all three observables:
      \[ J = \frac{\langle \Delta\Theta^2\rangle_w}{\mathrm{var}\,\Theta}
           + w_r\,\frac{\langle \Delta r^2\rangle_w}{\mathrm{var}\,r}
           + w_X\,\frac{\langle \Delta X^2\rangle_w}{\mathrm{var}\,X} \]
      \footnotesize
      dimensionless; 
      
      $\langle\cdot\rangle_w$: average with a weight $w_i$ per point.
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
      \small
      \begin{tabular}{cp{0.85\linewidth}}
        \toprule
        set & points, weights \\
        \midrule
        A & Zacharie-Aubrun + Onofri, standard UO$_2$; $w_i = 1$ \\
        B & all four papers; $w_i = 1$ \\
        C & as B, $w_i = \text{rank factor}\times\text{relevance}/3$ \\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}

      \vspace{0.4em}
      \footnotesize
      rank factor: A, B $\to 1$; U$^*$ $\to 0.5$; U $\to 0.25$.
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}

  \vspace{0.6em}
  \small
  Two questions:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{which weights} $w_r, w_X$? 
    \item \textbf{which data set}? 
  \end{enumerate}
\end{frame}

% =====================================================================
\section{Outlook: from a local functional to a phase field}
% =====================================================================

\begin{frame}{What a local functional cannot give -> phase-field models}
  \textbf{Problems of the Landau-like local functional}
  \small
  \begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{no spatial quantities};
    \item \textbf{no kinetics}: equilibrium is instantaneous.
  \end{itemize}

  \scriptsize
  \begin{tabular}{p{0.17\textwidth}p{0.44\textwidth}p{0.25\textwidth}}
    \toprule
    family & property & application/ref \\
    \midrule
    \textbf{KWC} 
     & two fields $(\phi,\theta)$, allows subgrain rotation; singular diffusion equations
     & Nucleation via subgrain coalescence, Muramatsu (2014) \\
    \textbf{MPF} 
     & One order parameter per grain; stable time increments; rotation ignored
     & Subgrain growth, Khajezade \emph{et al.} (2024) \\
    \textbf{HMP}
     & Removes nonphysical linear gradient term; handles inclination-dependent GB energy 
     & Coupled Cosserat crystal plasticity, Tandogan \emph{et al.} (2025); dislocation-driven nucleation, Tandogan \emph{et al.} (2026) \\
    \textbf{PFC} 
     & Atomic-resolution density field; diffusive timescales 
     & Interface morphology development during solidification, Nittala (2025) \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}

  \vspace{0.2em}
  \footnotesize
  Nucleation is usually \alert{seeded ad hoc} at a critical density or stress;
      spontaneous nucleation from lattice-curvature gradients is obtained when coupling KWC
      with Cosserat crystal plasticity (Ghiglione, 2024), and from stored dislocations at
      grain boundaries when coupling HMP with it (Tandogan, 2026).

\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Muramatsu \emph{et al.}~(2014): a KWC phase field for recrystallization}
  \footnotesize
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
      \textbf{The functional}\footnotemark[7] --- two fields, $\phi$ and $\theta$:
      \[ \mathcal{F} = \int_V \Big[\, f(\phi) + \tfrac{\alpha^2}{2}|\nabla\phi|^2
         + s\,g(\phi)\,|\nabla\theta| + \tfrac{\epsilon^2}{2}\,h(\phi)\,|\nabla\theta|^2
         \Big]\,\mathrm{d}V \]
      with $g(\phi) = h(\phi) = \phi^2$, relaxed by
      $\dot\phi = -M_\phi\,\delta\mathcal{F}/\delta\phi$ and
      $\dot\theta = -M_\theta\,\delta\mathcal{F}/\delta\theta$.

      $\phi = 1$ inside a subgrain; $\theta$ is the
      \textbf{lattice orientation}. 
      
      The \emph{singular} $|\nabla\theta|$ term gives a boundary
      an energy growing with misorientation.
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.44\textwidth}
      \textbf{The local part} (Eq.~7, $f_m = 0$):
      \[ f(\phi;E_s) = a_{ub}\big(1-p(\phi)\big)E_s + a_{wg}W_b\,q(\phi) \]
      \[ q(\phi) = \phi^2(1-\phi)^2 \]
      \[ p(\phi) = \phi^3(10-15\phi+6\phi^2) \]

        \scriptsize
      \begin{itemize}
        \item $q$: the \textbf{double well}, original matrix against new grains; its height $a_{wg}W_b$
          sets the boundary energy;
        \item $p$: is a sigmoid-like function where $p'(0)=p'(1)=0$m therefore it \emph{tilts} the well without
          moving its two minima;
        \item $E_s$: the \textbf{stored dislocation energy}, the only driving force, supplied
          from outside the model.
      \end{itemize}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \textbf{How the paper nucleates}: a subgrain group enclosed by high-angle ($>10^\circ$)
  boundaries is \emph{selected} as a nucleus candidate and grows after an \emph{incubation
  period} --- the criterion is \alert{imposed}, not produced by the free energy.
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Tandogan \emph{et al.}~(2026): nucleation \emph{from} the free energy}
  \footnotesize
      \begin{itemize}
      \item Recrystallization is usually modelled with an imposed nucleation (Muramatsu);
      \item Tandogan \emph{et al.}\footnotemark[8] obtain it spontaneously, from stored dislocations at grain boundaries through a one thermodynamically consistent field theory,
        Cosserat crystal plasticity $+$ Henry--Mellenthin--Plapp (HMP) orientation phase field (HMP-CCP).
    \end{itemize}

    \textbf{Order parameters}
    \begin{itemize}
      \item $\eta_{\text{T}}\in[0,1]$: coarse-grained \textbf{crystalline order}, $=1$ in
        the grain bulk, $<1$ inside the diffuse GB.
      \item $\theta$: lattice orientation, identified with the Cosserat microrotation
      \item 2D, small strain: dofs $(\eta_{\text{T}},\theta,u_1,u_2)$, FEniCS $+$
        Mfront.
    \end{itemize}

  \footnotetext[8]{Tandogan, Budnitzki, Sandfeld, \emph{J.\ Mech.\ Phys.\ Solids}
    \textbf{206} (2026) 106325. Presented here up to §3.2.}
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
\begin{frame}{The HMP-CCP free energy and the coupling function $\phi(\eta_{\text{T}})$}
  \footnotesize
  \[
    \psi = f_0\Big[\alpha V(\eta_{\text{T}}) + \tfrac{\nu^2}{2}|\nabla\eta_{\text{T}}|^2
      + \mu^2 g(\eta_{\text{T}})|\nabla\theta|^2\Big]
      + \tfrac12\,\boldsymbol{e}^e\!:\!\mathbb{E}\!:\!\boldsymbol{e}^e
      + 2\mu_c\big(\overset{\times}{e}{}^{e}\big)^2
      + \underbrace{\phi(\eta_{\text{T}})\sum_\alpha \tfrac{\lambda}{2}\mu b^2\rho_\alpha}_{\text{stored dislocations}}
  \]
  \vspace{-0.6em}

      \begin{itemize}
        \item $V = \tfrac12(1-\eta_{\text{T}})^2$: single well, penalises GBs.
        \item $g(\eta_{\text{T}})$ singular at 1, with a $\ln$ term $\Rightarrow$
          \textbf{Read--Shockley} GB energy.
        \item $\phi_{,\eta} = \tfrac{c_3}{2}\big[1-\tanh(c_1(\eta_{\text{T}}-c_2))\big]$: a
          \textbf{step}. The stored energy pushes on $\eta_{\text{T}}$ only inside the GB
          ($\eta_{\text{T}}<c_2$); the bulk is ``crystalline enough''.
        \item Recovery (Kocks--Mecking): extra sink $-\rho\,C_D A(\eta_{\text{T}})\,\dot\eta_{\text{T}}$,
          active only where $\dot\eta_{\text{T}}>0$: \textbf{behind a moving GB}.
      \end{itemize}

\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
\begin{frame}{Tandogan \emph{et al.}~(2026): all the equations}
  \scriptsize
  \begin{align*}
    \text{(32)}\;& \tau_\eta\dot\eta = f_0\nu^2\nabla^2\eta - f_0\big[\alpha V' + \mu^2 g'|\nabla\theta|^2\big] - \phi'\textstyle\sum_\alpha\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\mu_e r_\alpha^2
      \qquad (r_\alpha^2 \to b^2\rho_\alpha) \\
    \text{(33,34)}\;& 0 = f_0\nabla\!\cdot[\mu^2 g(\eta)\nabla\theta] + 2\mu_c e^e,\qquad -\tau_*\dot e_* = f_0\nabla\!\cdot[\mu^2 g\nabla\theta],\quad \tau_* = \hat\tau_* g(\eta)\ \text{(23)} \\
    \text{(30,31)}\;& \Omega_\eta = \tfrac12\tau_\eta^{-1}(\pi^{dis}_\eta)^2,\quad \pi^{dis}_\eta = -\tau_\eta\dot\eta \\
    \text{(35,36)}\;& V = \tfrac12(1-\eta)^2,\quad g = \tfrac{7\eta^3 - 6\eta^4}{(1-\eta)^3} + c\ln(1-\eta) + C_0,\quad
      C_0 = \min_{\eta_*}\big[\cdots\big] + 0.01,\ \ g(\min(\eta,1-10^{-4})) \\
    \text{(37,38)}\;& \phi(\eta) = \tfrac12 c_3\big\{\eta - c_1^{-1}\ln\cosh[c_1(c_2-\eta)]\big\} + c_0,\quad
      \phi'(\eta) = \tfrac{c_3}{2}\big[1 - \tanh(c_1(\eta - c_2))\big] \\
    \text{(28,29)}\;& \dot\rho_\alpha = \tfrac1b\big(K\sqrt{\textstyle\sum_\beta a_{\alpha\beta}\rho_\beta} - 2d\rho_\alpha\big)|\dot\gamma_\alpha| - \rho_\alpha C_D A(\eta)\dot\eta\ \ (\dot\eta > 0),\quad
      A = \tfrac{7\eta^3 - 6\eta^4}{1-\eta} \\
    \text{(41)}\;& f_{\eta1} = f_0\nu^2\nabla^2\eta,\ \ f_{\eta2} = -f_0\alpha V',\ \ f_{\eta3} = -f_0\mu^2 g'|\nabla\theta|^2,\ \ f_{\eta4} = -\phi'\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\mu_e b^2\rho \\
    \text{(42)}\;& \eta_{\text{eq}} = 1 - \dfrac{\phi'(\eta_{\text{eq}})\,\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\mu_e b^2\rho}{f_0\alpha},\quad \phi'(\eta_{\text{eq}}) = c_3\ \text{inside the widened GB}
  \end{align*}
  Table 1 (Cu): $f_0 = 371$\,kPa, $\alpha = 20$, $\nu = 1\,\mu$m, $\mu = 2.5/\pi\,\mu$m, $c = 3$, $\lambda = 0.3$,
  $b = 0.2556$\,nm, $C_D = 100$, $c_1/c_2/c_3 = 100/0.95/1.7$.
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
\begin{frame}{The nucleation mechanism: a Cu bicrystal}
  \footnotesize
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \begin{column}{0.4\textwidth}
      Periodic bicrystal, $\Delta\theta = 15^\circ$, uniform
      $\rho_0 = 2.5\times10^{15}$\,m$^{-2}$ switched on at $t=0$.

      \vspace{0.3em}
      \textbf{$C_D = 0$, no recovery}: the stored-energy force widens the GB into a
      non-localised orientation gradient, an \emph{unstable} state.

      \vspace{0.3em}
      \textbf{$C_D > 0$}: recovery at the GB centre: a dislocation-free nucleus
      bounded by two GBs that move outward.

    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.55\textwidth}
      \genfig[width=\textwidth]{tandogan_cu_fig4.png}

      \scriptsize
      Tandogan \emph{et al.}, Fig.~4: $\eta_{\text{T}}$, $\theta$, $\rho$ and the forces on
      $\eta_{\text{T}}$; red $C_D=0$, blue $C_D=100$.
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
\begin{frame}{Prototype: Tandogan in 1D, driven by the Landau model}
  \footnotesize
  \center
  \textbf{What is solved} --- one GB at $x = L/2$, $L = 10$\,µm, no load ($u = 0$, no
  slip, $\overset{\times}{e}{}^{e} = 0$):
  \begin{align*}
    \tau_\eta\,\dot\eta_{\text{T}} &= f_0\nu^2\eta_{\text{T}}''
      - f_0\big[\alpha V' + \mu^2 g'\,\theta'^2\big]
      - \phi_{,\eta}\,\tfrac{\lambda}{2}Gb^2\rho \\
    \hat\tau_*\,g\,\dot\theta &= f_0\,\big(\mu^2 g\,\theta'\big)' \\
    \dot\rho &= \alert{S(bu)} - \rho\,C_D\,A(\eta_{\text{T}})\,\langle\dot\eta_{\text{T}}\rangle
  \end{align*}
  \vspace{-0.8em}
  \begin{itemize}
    \item \alert{Irradiation source} instead of plasticity:
      $S = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}\rho_{\text{free}}}{\mathrm{d}bu}\,\dot{bu}$, uniform, independent of the
      local $\rho$ $\Rightarrow$ a recovered region is loaded again.
  \end{itemize}
  \textbf{From the Landau model}:
  \begin{itemize}
    \item $\Delta\theta \leftarrow \Theta(bu)$, $\rho \leftarrow \rho_{\text{free}}(bu)$
      (the random array = Tandogan's SSDs), $G(T)$, $b_{\text{UO}_2}$;
    \item  other parameters as in the paper
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\section{Open issues for discussion}
% =====================================================================

\begin{frame}{1. The sweep: linear $\Delta R/R$ or volume?}
  \small
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      \textbf{What changed}
      \begin{itemize}
        \item first version: $\rho_{\text{swept}} = (\rho_{\text{tot}}-\rho_{\text{ord}})\,\Delta R/R$,
          $r_n \propto 1+\Delta R/R$ --- linear in the sweep;
        \item now: Gourdet--Montheillet volume, $x = k\rho_{\text{ord}}/\rho_{\text{tot}}$,
          $\rho_{\text{swept}} \propto 1-e^{-x}$, $S/V \to S/V\,e^{-x}$.
      \end{itemize}
      \textbf{It matters}: $x\approx 0.5$ at 60\,GWd/tU, $e^{-x}=0.6$ against $1-x=0.5$.

      \vspace{0.3em}
      Geometry: a shell $\Delta R/R$ sweeps $1-(1-\Delta R/R)^3\approx 3\,\Delta R/R$ of the
      volume; radius as function of volume goes as $(1+x)^{1/3}$.
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.47\textwidth}
      \textbf{Literature}
      \begin{itemize}
        \item Gourdet \& Montheillet: $dV$ is a swept volume.
        \item Rest (2004--06): linear annulus depth $V_r = 1-[1-r/(d_g/2)]^3$, and the lattice
          strain $\Delta a/a_0$ as driving quantity.
      \end{itemize}
      \textbf{Questions}
      \begin{itemize}
        \item is $k\rho_{\text{ord}}/\rho_{\text{tot}}$ a length or a volume fraction?
        \item should the swept walls also leave the \emph{energy} ($\rho_{\text{ord}}\to\rho_{\text{ord}}e^{-x}$ in $F$)?
        \item sensitivity of $\Theta$, $X$, $r_n$ to the choice: one refit with the linear form.
      \end{itemize}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{2. Dataset differences: irradiation conditions and ranking}
  \scriptsize
  \begin{tabular}{p{0.16\textwidth}p{0.2\textwidth}p{0.28\textwidth}p{0.28\textwidth}}
    \toprule
    dataset & technique & conditions & observable \\
    \midrule
    Zacharie-Aubrun 2022 & EBSD, PWR & local burnup (model), grains 9--10\,$\mu$m std, 56--60\,$\mu$m Cr & $f_1$, $f_{10}$, AMis, ECD \\
    Onofri 2025 & EBSD $+$ TEM, 16 and 37 GWd/t & model burnup, grain size default & AMis, no $f_1$ \\
    Gerczak 2018 & SEM-BSE, EBSD, tKD, H.B.\ Robinson & burnup from literature (Barani) & rim $d_A$, area (rank U) \\
    Noirot 2015 & EPMA, Halden discs & enrichment 19.8\,\%, fission rate $\sim2\times$ PWR & Xe-depleted area \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}

  \vspace{0.4em}
  \footnotesize
  \begin{itemize}
    \item Each dataset has \textbf{its own irradiation conditions}, and is already ranked
      differently: $w = f(\text{Rose rank})\times\text{relevance}/3$ (Zacharie std carries about 70\,\% of the fraction weight).
    \item Different observables are fitted as one ``fraction'' (EBSD $f_{10}$, Xe-depleted area,
      BSE image analysis); $\Theta$ is $T$-independent while centre points ($\sim 900\,^\circ$C) and
      rim points ($\sim 400\,^\circ$C) sit at the same burnup.
    \item At 35\,GWd/t: AMis $0.4$--$0.7^\circ$ (Onofri) against $0.9^\circ$ (Zacharie); the model gives 0 for both.
  \end{itemize}
  \textbf{To discuss}: is rank $\times$ relevance enough, or should the weight depend on
  $T$, fission rate, enrichment (a condition-aware rank, or a per-dataset onset offset)?
  Leave-one-dataset-out fits show the sensitivity. And: use the \emph{previous formation curves}
  (options 1--3) as extra, low-weight calibration targets for $X(bu)$? Risk: circular, they are
  fits of the same biased data.
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{3. Critical densities}
  \small
  \begin{center}
  \begin{tabular}{lr}
    \toprule
    source & value \\
    \midrule
    this model, $\rho_{\text{crit}}$ & $6.85\times10^{14}$\,m$^{-2}$ (47.1\,GWd/tU on the Nogita line) \\
    Nogita \& Une (1994), measured & $5.8\times10^{14}$ at 44, $6.0\times10^{14}$ at 83\,GWd/t \\
    Veshchunov \& Shestak (2009) & $6\times10^{14}$ to $\sim10^{15}$\,m$^{-2}$ \\
    Matzke \& Kinoshita (1997) & $\sim70$\,GWd/t local \\
    Sontheimer (2011) & 75\,GWd/tU \\
    model: $X>0$ & 52.3\,GWd/tU \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
  \end{center}
  \footnotesize
  \begin{itemize}
    \item The Veshchunov value is \alert{not independent}: it is Nogita's datum at 44\,GWd/t, and $\rho_{\text{crit}}$ is Eq.~(1) at 47.
    \item Eq.~(1) extrapolated to 83\,GWd/t gives $4.2\times10^{15}$ against $6.0\times10^{14}$ measured.
    \item Onofri's TEM line density, $1.1\times10^{13}$ and $0.8\times10^{13}$\,m$^{-2}$ at 16 and 37\,GWd/t, is $10$--$50\times$
      below Eq.~(1) and nearly burnup-independent.
    \item $A_1$ uses the \emph{excess} density $\rho_N-\rho_{\text{crit}}$ ($3.5\times10^{12}$ at 47.2\,GWd/tU), not the real one ($\sim7\times10^{14}$).
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{4. Phase-field functions for the HBS formation, and the problems met}
  \scriptsize
  \begin{tabular}{p{0.16\textwidth}p{0.26\textwidth}p{0.26\textwidth}p{0.22\textwidth}}
    \toprule
     & Muramatsu (KWC) & Tandogan (HMP-CCP) & Landau (here) \\
    \midrule
    order parameter & $\phi$ nucleus/matrix, $\theta$ & $\eta$ crystal/boundary, $\theta$ & $\eta=\theta/\theta_{\max}$, mean field \\
    role of $\rho$ & $E_s=\rho\mu b^2/2$ tilts $f(\phi)$ & $\phi(\eta)\rho b^2$ tilts $\eta$ in the GB only & $\rho_{\text{tot}}$ split in 3 populations \\
    threshold & $r^*=2\gamma_b/E_s$, criteria (11),(13), imposed & $\eta_{\text{eq}}<1$, then recovery $A(\eta)$ & $\rho_{\text{crit}}$ \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}

  \vspace{0.4em}
  \footnotesize
  \textbf{Problems of the 1D UO$_2$ prototype}
  \begin{itemize}
    \item \emph{width}: $\nu=2.5\,\mu$m (GB width $\sim5\,\mu$m) against subgrains of $0.2$--$0.8\,\mu$m: the smallest feature is not resolved;
    \item \emph{onset is an input}: $c_3 = 2.659$ is fitted to nucleate at 60\,GWd/tU; $\eta_{\text{eq}}<0$ beyond $\sim81$\,GWd/tU;
    \item Cu parameters, placeholder time scale, $C_D=10$ instead of 100, no thermal activation;
    \item \emph{nothing makes misorientation}: $\eta,\theta$ redistribute the parent angles, so $\Theta(bu)$ is not reproduced; 1D has no curvature;
    \item archived prototype: $\nu=50$\,nm, $f_0=10.8$\,MPa and a Read--Shockley target $\sim35\,\%$ above Zhang (1.59 against $1.18$\,J/m$^2$ at $10^\circ$).
  \end{itemize}
  \textbf{Which free-energy function} should carry $\rho$, and where does the threshold come from?
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Backup --- the equations}
  \scriptsize
  \begin{align*}
    \text{(1)}\;\; & \rho_{\text{tot}}(bu) = \max\!\big(10^{2.2\times10^{-2} bu + 13.8}-\rho_{\text{crit}},\,0\big) \\
    \text{(2)}\;\; & G(T,P,x,q),\ \nu(T,P,x,q) \quad \text{NEA/NSC/R(2024)1 p.\ 124};\quad f(\nu) = \tfrac{1-\nu/2}{1-\nu} \\
    \text{(3)}\;\; & \rho^{\max}_{\text{LAGB}} = \Big(\tfrac{3n\theta_{\max}}{\beta b}\Big)^2,\quad
                     (S/V)_{\max} = \tfrac{9n\theta_{\max}}{\beta^2 b},\quad
                     x_{\max} = \tfrac{k\,\rho^{\max}_{\text{LAGB}}}{\rho_{\text{tot}}} \\
    \text{(4)}\;\; & A_1 = \tfrac{f(\nu)}{4\pi}\ln\tfrac{\rho_{\text{tot}}^{-1/2}}{b},\qquad
                     A_2 = \tfrac{f(\nu)}{4\pi}\ln\tfrac{\min(b/\theta,\,\rho_{\text{tot}}^{-1/2})}{b} \\
    \text{(5)}\;\; & \rho_{\text{ord}} = \rho^{\max}_{\text{LAGB}}\eta^2,\ \ x = x_{\max}\eta^2,\ \
                     \rho_{\text{free}} = (\rho_{\text{tot}}-\rho_{\text{ord}})e^{-x},\ \
                     \rho_{\text{swept}} = (\rho_{\text{tot}}-\rho_{\text{ord}})(1-e^{-x}) \\
    \text{(6)}\;\; & F = \rho_{\text{free}}A_1Gb^2 + \rho_{\text{ord}}A_2Gb^2 = C_0 + E_{\text{wall}} + E_{\text{sweep}} \\
    \text{(7,7b)}\;& \eta_{\text{eq}} = \operatorname{argmin}_{[0,\min(\eta_{\text{bal}},1)]}F,\quad
                     \eta_{\text{bal}} = \sqrt{\min(\rho_{\text{tot}}/\rho^{\max}_{\text{LAGB}},1)} \\
    \text{(8)}\;\; & \Theta = \min(\eta_{\text{eq}}\theta_{\max}\cdot\tfrac{180}{\pi},\ \theta_{\text{HAGB}}) \\
    \text{(9)}\;\; & r_n = \min\!\big(\tfrac{1.5}{(S/V)_{\max}\,\eta\,e^{-x}},\ R_{\text{grain}}\big) \\
    \text{(10)}\;\;& X = \mathrm{clip}\big(\tfrac{\Theta-\theta_u}{\theta_{\text{HAGB}}-\theta_u},\,0,\,1-10^{-9}\big)
  \end{align*}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Backup --- regimes and parameters}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      \textbf{Regimes} ($T$-, $P$-, $x$-independent)
      \small
      \begin{tabular}{lr}
        \toprule
        condition & $bu$ [GWd/tU] \\
        \midrule
        $\rho_{\text{tot}} > 0$, $\Theta$ leaves 0 & 47.09 \\
        $\Theta = \theta_u$, $X$ leaves 0 & 52.27 \\
        $\Theta = \theta_{\text{HAGB}}$   & 109.96 \\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}

      \vspace{0.8em}
      With the shipped set-C parameters the balance bound of Eq.~(7b) \textbf{binds from 89 to 110\,GWd/tU}; below it $\eta$ is the interior minimum of Eq.~(7).
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      \textbf{Fixed constants}
      \small
      \begin{tabular}{lr}
        \toprule
        $b$ & 3.889e-10 m \\
        $\theta_{\max}$ & $= \theta_{\text{HAGB}}$ \\
        $\theta_{\text{HAGB}}$ & $10^\circ$ \\
        $\theta_u$ & $1.00^\circ$ \\
        $n$ & 2 \\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}

      \vspace{0.6em}
      \footnotesize
      $\theta_u$ is the lower end member of the mixture Eq.~(10) inverts, and it is set by
      the \textbf{measurement convention}, not fitted: the EBSD data reports a restructured
      fraction \emph{at} $1^\circ$ ($f_1$) and one \emph{at} $10^\circ$ ($f_{10}$), so
      $1^\circ$ is the edge below which a boundary is not counted at all. A map whose whole
      resolved population sits there carries no restructuring --- which is $X = 0$.
      It fixes only \emph{where} $X$ leaves zero: $\Theta$ and $r_n$ do not depend on it.
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Backup --- the 1D HMP prototype: implemented equations}
  \scriptsize
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \begin{column}{0.55\textwidth}
      \textbf{Fields} $\eta_{\text{T}}(x,t)$, $\theta(x,t)$, $\rho(x,t)$ on $x\in[0,L]$, one GB at $L/2$;
      $u=0$, no slip, $\theta=-e^*$ (Eq.~27)
      \begin{align*}
        \text{(32)}\;\; & \tau_\eta\,\dot\eta_{\text{T}} = f_0\nu^2\eta_{\text{T}}''
          - f_0\big[\alpha V'(\eta_{\text{T}}) + \mu^2 g'(\eta_{\text{T}})\,\theta'^2\big]
          - \phi'(\eta_{\text{T}})\,\tfrac{\lambda}{2}Gb^2\rho \\
        \text{(34)}\;\; & \hat\tau\, g(\eta_{\text{T}})\,\dot\theta
          = f_0\,\big(\mu^2 g(\eta_{\text{T}})\,\theta'\big)' \\
        \text{(28)}\;\; & \dot\rho = S(bu) - \rho\, C_D\, A(\eta_{\text{T}})\,\langle\dot\eta_{\text{T}}\rangle,
          \qquad \langle\cdot\rangle = \max(\cdot,0)
      \end{align*}
      \vspace{-1.2em}
      \begin{align*}
        & V = \tfrac12(1-\eta_{\text{T}})^2,\qquad
          A = \frac{7\eta_{\text{T}}^3-6\eta_{\text{T}}^4}{1-\eta_{\text{T}}} \\
        & g = \frac{7\eta_{\text{T}}^3-6\eta_{\text{T}}^4}{(1-\eta_{\text{T}})^3}
            + c\ln(1-\eta_{\text{T}}) + g_{\text{off}},\quad \min g = 0.01 \\
        & \phi' = \tfrac{c_3}{2}\big[1-\tanh\big(c_1(\eta_{\text{T}}-c_2)\big)\big] \\
        \text{(42)}\;\; & \eta_{\text{T}}^{\text{eq}} = 1 - \frac{c_3\,\tfrac{\lambda}{2}Gb^2\rho}{f_0\,\alpha}
      \end{align*}
      $g$, $g'$, $A$ frozen for $\eta_{\text{T}} > 1-10^{-4}$; $\eta_{\text{T}}'=\theta'=0$ at $x=0,L$.
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.43\textwidth}
      \textbf{Coupling to the Landau model}, \texttt{hbs\_state($bu$,$T$)}
      \[
        \Delta\theta = \Theta(bu),\qquad \rho \leftarrow \rho_{\text{free}}(bu),\qquad G = G(T,\dots)
      \]
      \[
        c_3 = \frac{(1-0.579)\,f_0\,\alpha}{\tfrac{\lambda}{2}Gb^2\,\rho_{\text{free}}(bu_{\text{sat}})}
      \]
      so that Eq.~(42) gives the paper's Cu value $0.579$ where $\Theta=\theta_{\text{HAGB}}$.

      \vspace{0.4em}
      \textbf{Two protocols for $\rho$}
      \begin{itemize}
        \item \emph{step}: $S=0$, $\rho(x,0)=\rho_{\text{free}}(bu)$ (as in §3.2);
        \item \emph{irradiation}: $\rho(x,0)=0$,
          $S = \dfrac{d\rho_{\text{ref}}}{d\,bu}\,\dot{bu}$, uniform in $x$,
          $\rho_{\text{ref}}\in\{\rho_{\text{free}},\rho_{\text{tot}}\}$,
          $bu = bu_0 + \dot{bu}\,t$ (compressed).
      \end{itemize}

      \vspace{0.2em}
      \textbf{Nucleus}: $\rho(L/2) < 0.1\,\rho_0$ while $\min\eta_{\text{T}}(0,L) > c_2$.
      \textbf{Capillarity} (absent in 1D): $r^* = 2\gamma\big/\big(\tfrac{\lambda}{2}Gb^2\rho\big)$.

      \vspace{0.2em}
      Interface parameters: Cu, Table~1 ($f_0,\nu,\alpha,\mu,c,\tau_\eta,\hat\tau,C_D$), not calibrated for UO$_2$.
      FV, 400 cells, BDF.
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}
